findings.title: D-042 made anchor 1 unconditional and updated the checkClosure comment, but the commitPresent() header comment still describes anchor 1 as conditional ('when it resolves; this findManifest tolerance covers the one case it may not'). Two comments in rules.mjs now contradict each other about the closure guarantee
findings.reproduction: At 7edacdc, tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:602-605 (the header comment above commitPresent) says: 'the fix must be an ancestor of THREE anchors -- the verifying round's frozen source_commit (when it resolves; this findManifest tolerance covers the one case it may not), the verifying run's real head, and the gate candidate'. The code it describes, rules.mjs:746-749, now rejects outright a closure verified in a round whose source_commit does not resolve ('... is not present; a closure must be verified against a retained candidate (F-DG0-169)'). The new checkClosure comment (:726-741) says the same. My round-25 finding F-DG0-169 named this exact comment in its 'expected' (c): 'correct the comments at rules.mjs:603-605 and :737-738'. D-042 corrected the checkClosure comment but left :603-605. Command: git show 7edacdc:tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs | sed -n 597,605p (output with line numbers in docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-26/stale-comment.log). Behaviour is unaffected: SEC26-1 and SEC26-2 in sec26-repro.log show that the absent-source case is rejected.
findings.expected: Every comment in rules.mjs describes anchor 1 the way the code enforces it: unconditionally, with a closure verified in an absent-source round rejected. Suggested wording at :603-605: 'the verifying round's frozen source_commit (which must be present: a closure verified in a round whose source_commit does not resolve is rejected, D-042), the verifying run's real head, and the gate candidate'. D-042's text is already accurate.
findings.actual: The header comment still reads as though anchor 1 is skipped for an absent-source round. That was the pre-D-042 behaviour. A reader auditing the validator from that comment would underestimate the guarantee and could misjudge a future change to this code. Impact is documentation accuracy only: no gate outcome depends on it, and the code and its test (validator.test.mjs 'D-042 / F-DG0-169') are correct. This is the same class as F-DG0-167/F-DG0-014, a stale comment after a validator change, recorded at Low under threat-model.md.
